metadata.technology_reasoning: Automatic capsule filling machines are the industry-standard equipment used globally for mass production of pharmaceutical capsules, widely adopted due to their efficiency, accuracy, and ability to handle large volumes with consistent dosing.

components.reasoning: The material feeding unit holding powder or granules to be filled into capsules is a standard primary component.
Core mechanism that accurately measures and dispenses the fill material into capsule halves, distinct and critical for dosing precision.
Subassembly that orients and supplies empty capsules into the machine for filling, universally required as a separate module.
Where the dosing system deposits the fill into capsule bodies; primary functional part assembled separately or clearly defined.
Component or module that joins capsule bodies with caps, essential as a separate assembly in most machines.
Electronic interface for machine operation control and monitoring, typically a separate purchased unit in automatic machines.
Mechanical system that powers the machine operation and coordinate motion, always present and supplied as a distinct subassembly.
The main structural assembly supporting all modules, procured or manufactured as a distinct unit.

Hopper.name: Stainless steel
Hopper.reasoning: Stainless steel is widely used for hoppers in capsule filling machines due to its corrosion resistance, strength, and hygienic properties essential for pharmaceutical processing; this is an industry standard with very few substitutes.

Hopper.name: Aluminum
Hopper.reasoning: Aluminum may be used as a lightweight alternative for non-critical hopper parts, offering corrosion resistance but less commonly used than stainless steel, representing a moderate confidence.

Dosator or Dosing System.name: Stainless steel
Dosator or Dosing System.reasoning: Dosing components require food-grade, corrosion-resistant metal; stainless steel is the industry standard for durability and hygiene in contact with powders.

Dosator or Dosing System.name: Aluminum
Dosator or Dosing System.reasoning: Sometimes used for dosing parts where weight savings are needed; less common but possible alternative.

Dosator or Dosing System.name: PTFE
Dosator or Dosing System.reasoning: PTFE is used as a coating or sealant on moving parts for its low friction and chemical resistance, improving functionality; common but alternatives like other polymers exist.

Capsule Feeding System.name: Stainless steel
Capsule Feeding System.reasoning: Structural and mechanical parts in capsule feeding systems usually require stainless steel for corrosion resistance and strength.

Capsule Feeding System.name: Aluminum
Capsule Feeding System.reasoning: May be used for some lightweight parts or housings, but less common than stainless steel.

Capsule Feeding System.name: PTFE
Capsule Feeding System.reasoning: Used for coatings or low friction surfaces in feeding mechanisms; common but some alternatives exist.

Filling Station.name: Stainless steel
Filling Station.reasoning: The filling station contacts powder or capsules directly and requires corrosion resistant, hygienic materials; stainless steel is widely used and essential.

Filling Station.name: Aluminum
Filling Station.reasoning: Sometimes used for non-contact or structural parts for weight savings but less critical than stainless steel.

Filling Station.name: PTFE
Filling Station.reasoning: Used for coatings on surfaces needing low friction or chemical resistance, common but substitutable.

Closing Station.name: Stainless steel
Closing Station.reasoning: Closing station components require durability and corrosion resistance; stainless steel is standard and critical for machine function.

Closing Station.name: Aluminum
Closing Station.reasoning: May be used in less critical components for weight saving but less common than stainless steel.

Control Panel (HMI).name: Silicon
Control Panel (HMI).reasoning: Silicon is the fundamental semiconductor material used in all electronic circuits of the control panel.

Control Panel (HMI).name: Copper
Control Panel (HMI).reasoning: Copper is used for electrical wiring and PCB traces due to excellent conductivity, universally essential.

Control Panel (HMI).name: Glass
Control Panel (HMI).reasoning: Glass is commonly used as substrate or protective cover for displays and touchscreens.

Control Panel (HMI).name: Aluminum
Control Panel (HMI).reasoning: Aluminum is often used for housing frames and heat sinks in control panels, common but alternatives like steel exist.

Control Panel (HMI).name: Polycarbonate
Control Panel (HMI).reasoning: Polycarbonate is a polymer used for display screens and protective covers; alternatives exist but it is widely used.

Drive System (Motor and Transmission).name: Copper
Drive System (Motor and Transmission).reasoning: Copper is essential for motor windings providing electrical conductivity, universally necessary.

Drive System (Motor and Transmission).name: Steel Ingots
Drive System (Motor and Transmission).reasoning: Steel is the primary material for structural motor parts and transmissions; steel ingots relate to steel material supply.

Drive System (Motor and Transmission).name: Aluminum
Drive System (Motor and Transmission).reasoning: Aluminum is commonly used for motor housings and some transmission parts to reduce weight; alternatives exist but common.

Frame and Structural Platform.name: Steel Ingots
Frame and Structural Platform.reasoning: The frame and platform require strong structural material; steel from steel ingots is standard and critical.

Frame and Structural Platform.name: Aluminum
Frame and Structural Platform.reasoning: Aluminum may be used for lightweight frame parts or panels but less common than steel for structural components.

Frame and Structural Platform.name: Stainless steel
Frame and Structural Platform.reasoning: Some high-end frames utilize stainless steel for corrosion resistance, less common but possible.
